earlier_scan.source_named: Lorrain, R.A. 1951. Grammar and Dictionary of the Lakher or Mara Language — not online; Savidge 1908 (archive.org) was read but contains only an orthographic accent-mark note, no word-stress description

sources.citation: Savidge, Fred W. 1908. A grammar and dictionary of the Lakher language. Allahabad: Pioneer Press. 225 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only 'Lakher alphabet and pronunciation' (pp. 1-2, page images viewed). Footnote to the asterisked long vowels â ê î ô û: '* The final vowels of words and syllables being generally long, they are not as a rule accented.' — 'accented' here means marked with the circumflex length sign (orthography), not word stress. No word-stress description; no tones recognised.

sources.citation: Löffler, Lorenz G. 2002. Some notes on Maraa. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 25(1): 123-136. doi:10.15144/LTBA-25.1.123
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §2 'Phonemes and tones' (pp. 124-127): Maraa has three tones (low, high, mid), 'both Savidge and Lorrain failed to recognize the importance of tones'; 'Lorrain mentions them in his Grammar and Dictionary, but the tones he gives in the few lines devoted to this (p. 59) are mostly wrong' (p. 125). The only 'stress' mentions concern the diphthong /ie/: 'the only diphthong in Maraa with the stress on the second vowel; a Frenchman would have written it /ié/' (p. 126) and 'MM /ie/ (with the stress on a very narrow [e])' (p. 133) — vowel-internal prominence, not word stress. No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Arden, Michelle J. 2010. A phonetic, phonological, and morphosyntactic analysis of the Mara language. MA thesis, San Jose State University (Master's Theses 3744). doi:10.31979/etd.v36r-dk3u. 179 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Nothing. a full-text search for stress/accent yields only non-phonological uses (e.g. 'stress that these early researchers..'). Phonology chapters (5 'Phonetic Inventory', 6 'Contrastive Sounds') describe segments and a tone system: 'The Mara language is primarily a three-tone system, although some exceptions exist.. There is ample evidence that all three tones are contrastive' (§5.3, p. 49); 'Mara has predominantly three tones.. Tonal contrast is evident' (§6.3, p. 63); §6.3.1 falling contour tones (pp. 64-66). No section on stress, prominence or word-level accent. Sabeu dialect (consultant…

sources.citation: Lorrain, Reginald Arthur. 1951. Grammar and dictionary of the Lakher or Mara language. Gauhati: Government of Assam, Dept. of Historical and Antiquarian Studies. x+372 pp. — ONLY 3 pages (title, introduction, Part I Orthography) as scanned by the Rosetta Project
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 1286.180); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Part I Orthography: alphabet, 'All syllables in the Mara language end in a vowel never in a consonant'; 'All the ordinary vowels in Mara.. being long there are only a very few instances where the vowel needs a circumflex accent placed over it to increase the length of that sound' — circumflex 'accent' = vowel length, with a minimal pair of meaning change; nothing on word stress. The full grammar (pp. 1-59; Löffler reports a few lines on tones at p. 59) is not open: HathiTrust catalog lists it 'Limited (search only)'; not on archive.org, Google Books, or DLI.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mara language' (accessed 2026-09-17) — used only as a pointer to sources
sources.note: Phonology section covers consonants and vowels only; nothing on tone or stress; cites Arden 2010 and Savidge 1908.

sources.citation: VanBik, Kenneth. 2009. Proto-Kuki-Chin: A reconstructed ancestor of the Kuki-Chin languages. STEDT Monograph 8. Berkeley: UC Berkeley. 626 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative-historical; Mara (Maraic group, §2.3.3, pp. 22-23) treated via sound correspondences (initials, rhymes, tones). a full-text search for stress/accent finds only lexical glosses (e.g. [1292] INTONATION/ACCENT PCC *thluuk, Mara thlu-zi 'a tune'). No statement on Mara word stress.

sources.citation: Löffler, Lorenz G. 2004. Some notes on Maraa: II. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 27(1): 61-87. doi:10.15144/LTBA-27.1.61

sources.note: Dialect comparison (Tlongsai vs. Sabeu/Fabau), tones and sandhi contours, prefixes, reconstruction. No mention of stress or accent at all (a full-text search for stress/accent 27 scanned pages).
